run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded, SEARCH-ONLY run. The hard egress constraint seen on recent runs persisted: the session network policy denied all direct HTTPS to tender hosts (WebFetch returned DNS ENOTFOUND for www.tenders.gov.au, and per environment guidance no further direct fetches were attempted once the failure mode was confirmed). No buyer-originated portal, detail page, feed/API or tender document could be opened; discovery was limited to the WebSearch tool (US-indexed, returning predominantly cached snapshots and third-party aggregator pages). Because WebSearch's index lags the run date, the overwhelming majority of surfaced opportunities had already passed their closing date and were excluded rather than captured. Tier 1 (AusTender; NSW buy.nsw / eTendering; VIC Buying for Victoria; QLD Brisbane; WA Tenders WA; SA/TAS; NT QTOL; ACT) swept by search. Tier 2 (local government via VendorPanel and council sites; universities/TAFEs; water corporations - Sydney/Melbourne/SA Water; GBEs - Western Power, Port of Melbourne, Westport, Perth Airport, Ports North; public health districts) swept by search. Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network; BHP/Rio/Fortescue/Woodside; EstimateOne construction; major retail/bank/telco) checked by search - every corporate channel remained registration-gated or invitation-only with no publicly-visible open RFx; recorded as portals only, none fabricated. Net result: NO new, independently-verifiable, currently-open opportunity could be captured this run. Four still-open, buyer-corroborated carryover opportunities were re-confirmed via this run's searches and are re-asserted under their existing dedup_keys with current_status updated (NSW Government ~$80M Master Media RFT closing 27 Nov 2026, re-confirmed via trade press; two Brisbane City Council construction tenders closing 7 and 11 Dec 2026; the Transport for NSW New England Highway Maitland Westbound ROI closing 11 Dec 2026). All four are carried at headline level only - deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, submission mechanics, values and contacts are null because the buyer detail pages and documents could not be opened. Three genuinely new sources were identified and recorded (Infrastructure Australia contracts/tenders page; Banana Shire Council QLD tenders; Utility Magazine open-tenders board as a low-confidence discovery signal). No opportunity, deliverable, date, value or contact was fabricated.
gaps: HARD EGRESS BLOCK (unchanged from recent runs): all direct HTTPS to tender hosts is denied by the session network policy. WebFetch returned DNS ENOTFOUND for www.tenders.gov.au and the same failure mode applies to every other buyer portal, so no buyer-originated detail page, feed/API or tender document could be opened this run. To restore full discovery, at minimum these hosts should be allowed in the session network settings: www.tenders.gov.au, buy.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au / supply.qld.gov.au, www.tenders.wa.gov.au, www.tenders.sa.gov.au, www.tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, www.tenders.act.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au, service.ariba.com, www.brisbane.qld.gov.au, estimateone.com, and individual council/university/utility/corporate sites.

Every tender captured this run is headline-only and UNVERIFIED on the buyer's own page. Titles, reference numbers and closing dates come from WebSearch snippets of trade press and aggregator/buyer pages, not from an opened buyer detail page. Deliverables, requirements, eligibility, evaluation criteria, submission mechanics, value and contacts are therefore null and still need a detail pass once egress is restored.

WebSearch index lags the run date (2026-11-16). Almost all surfaced notices had already closed - e.g. TfNSW Mona Vale Road West EOI (closed 11 Sep 2026), Palladium/DFAT 'Ports of the Future' RFT26-001 EOI (closed 13 Sep 2026), Westport Program Management & Commercial Services Panel EOI (closed 19 Mar 2026), Western Power WP2600150 Housing & Infrastructure Growth EOI (closed 20 Aug 2026), Port of Melbourne Port Rail Transformation infrastructure-works EOI (marked closed). All were correctly excluded, NOT captured. Genuinely recent (last 24-48h) buyer-originated notices are almost certainly undercounted this run.

Tier 3 corporate (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Woodside, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, major banks/telcos, EstimateOne) remained registration-gated or invitation-only; no authenticated supplier session is available, so no corporate opportunity could be read. Recorded as portals only; no corporate tender fabricated. Management-consultancy / invitation-only RFPs are out of scope by definition and were not invented.

The four re-asserted opportunities are carryovers from earlier runs (existing dedup_keys) that were re-confirmed as still open via this run's searches; they were not freshly discovered this run. No new, independently-verifiable, currently-open opportunity was found.
recommended_seed_additions: Infrastructure Australia - Contracts and Tenders (https://www.infrastructureaustralia.gov.au/about/contracts-and-tenders) - buyer-originated Commonwealth statutory-body procurement page; not previously in the known-source set.

Banana Shire Council (QLD) - Tenders and Quotations (https://www.banana.qld.gov.au/Online-Services/Find/Tenders-and-Quotations) - buyer-originated local-government tenders page publishing via VendorPanel; not previously in the known-source set.

Utility Magazine - Open Tenders and Opportunities (https://utilitymagazine.com.au/category/news/open-tenders-and-opportunities/) - industry-news board surfacing water/energy/utility tenders; LOW confidence as a buyer-originated source, useful only as a free DISCOVERY SIGNAL to pivot to the named utility buyer's own supplier portal.

Once egress is restored, open the buyer detail pages for the four carried opportunities (buy.nsw NSW Master Media RFT; Brisbane City Council Doc118000917 and Doc115483155; TfNSW 26.0000139291.0941.ROI) and complete the deliverables/requirements detail pass.

discovered_sources.source_name: Utility Magazine - Open Tenders and Opportunities
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Surfaced via WebSearch for water-utility tenders; an industry-news board that lists open water/energy/utility tenders and EOIs.
discovered_sources.notes: NOT a buyer-originated portal - it is a free industry-news DISCOVERY SIGNAL only. Use it to spot utility buyers and then pivot to the named utility's own supplier portal (e.g. Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, SA Water, Western Power). Low confidence by design; never treat as a source of truth.

discovered_sources.source_name: SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery
discovered_sources.how_discovered: Mandatory Tier-3 check each run. Confirmed via WebSearch that SAP Business Network Discovery remains the public posting board where buyers post open RFx, and that multiple Australian buyers (councils, utilities such as Endeavour Energy, Synergy, Western Power) run sourcing through Ariba.
discovered_sources.notes: Registration-gated: a free supplier account is required to view full opportunity detail. No authenticated session available this run, so no individual Ariba opportunity could be read. Recorded as a portal; no corporate tender fabricated.
